question: Should WhatsApp adopt the canonical rule that injected media readers require explicit local roots, while making the focused base64 and media capabilities part of the public Plugin SDK?
rationale: The implementation appears correct, but accepting a fail-closed change for existing injected-reader callers and committing to new public SDK surface requires owner intent rather than automated judgment.

options.title: Approve canonical boundary
options.body: Accept the explicit-root requirement and additive SDK contract as the intended secure upgrade behavior, then merge after exact-head checks finish.

options.title: Preserve affected callers first
options.body: Audit shipped injected-reader callers and update any rootless integrations to provide explicit boundaries before landing the refactor.

recommendation.title: Approve canonical boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the explicit-root requirement and additive SDK contract as the intended secure upgrade behavior, then merge after exact-head checks finish.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent shared media-access and Plugin SDK boundary work most directly defines both decisions.
